newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest share market extends rally, BUX hits high.
newsitem.headline: Budapest share market extends rally, BUX hits high.

text.p: The Budapest bourse hit a new high on Tuesday as many investors were seen in a hurry to buy stocks ahead of an expected new spurt after a predicted decision by the U.S. Fed to leave its rates steady.
The market outperformed advancing European bourses as the BUX index closed at a second successive record high of 5,686.69 points, up 113.89.
"Investors brought forward some purchases ahead of the Fed meeting believing the Fed won't raise interest rates," said Istvan Imrich of IBB Securities.
"In the absence of a rate hike, investors' appetite will rise further, but I would warn investors to be cautious as the rise can be expected to stop."
However, the BUX futures market reflected optimism, with all maturities closing sharply higher, by between 101.50 and 210.00 points. The March 1997 maturity finished at 6,060 points, up 130.00.
On the spot market certain stocks benefited from bullish expectations of their annual results, traders said.
Hotel firm Danubius surged to a new record level of 5,570 forints, before closing at 5,520, up 280, in not particularly strong volume.
"I think these prices reflect investors' expectations of the company's annual results," one trader said earlier today, adding that Danubius has a good track record of confirming expectations.
The day's most actively traded paper, oil and gas company MOL, jumped to a new record high of 3,600 forints.
Traders attributed the rise to expectations of an attractive pricing for a new tranche of MOL shares which they believe will go on sale later this month.
"The (upcoming) privatisation is moving MOL's price," said Imrich. MOL closed at 3,595 forints, up 125.
Chemicals firm Borsodchem firmed four and a half percent by close but came down from a daily peak of 6,315 forints.
Traders said Borsodchem benefited from low prices rather than from news of planned new factories. Borsodchem closed at 6,250 forints, up 270.
